articles.title: The drone-delivery boom could be a nightmare for people traumatized by war
articles.summary: In August, Amazon announced plans to expand its Prime Air delivery drone program to “ nearly 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026." Combined with similar uncrewed aerial delivery programs from DoorDash and Zipline (in partnership with Uber and Walmart), the expansion suggests that flying robots…
body: For many people, delivery drones will be little more than a novelty, occasionally good for a laugh when one does something ridiculous. For others, though, their growing use could be a nightmare. As the instant delivery industry clears the last FAA hurdles to rapid deliveries beyond an operator's line of sight, an increasing number of people worldwide are living with post-traumatic stress disorder or other anxiety-related disorders triggered by drones.

The use of all manner of weaponized drones in the ongoing war in Ukraine and in Israeli attacks on Lebanon and Gaza has already produced an epidemic of what some mental health professionals have dubbed “dronophobia. ” And while relatively few US troops have been targeted by drones flown by Iran, ISIS, and Iran-backed militias throughout the Middle East, even those who have not directly been attacked may experience anxiety simply because of the ample video footage of attacks circulating in news and social media.

articles.title: Elon Musk joins 165,000 others calling for Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang in open letter
articles.summary: CEO ousted after affair with suspected Chinese spy reportedly plans comeback, as US treasury secretary urges ‘dramatic shake-up’ Megaspeed says it’s a ‘legitimate and lawful business’ Business live – latest updates.
body: Elon Musk and a host of other tech bosses have called for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia, amid reports the former chief executive is already plotting a return to the chip company just four days after his resignation.
An open letter, which has more than 165,000 signatories, demands that the company’s board members “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts”.

Huang’s resignation on Thursday ended a 33-year run at the helm of the AI company he co-founded, after reports he had at least two extramarital affairs, one with a woman accused of spying for China and another with a subordinate.

According to the Financial Times, Huang has discussed a possible return to the company with people close to him. One Huang ally told the paper they were putting together ⁠a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby ​for the former Nvidia ‌CEO’s return ‌and would try to garner support from ‌the White House.

articles.title: Albanese treads tightrope in upcoming Trump meeting, wanting Indo-Pacific engagement and end to Iran and Ukraine wars
articles.summary: Quad leaders’ summit in Philippines is Trump’s first, as Australia joins US and Japan to protect AI technologies in face of China efforts to dominate. Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: Anthony Albanese will attempt to walk a tightrope in his relationship with Donald Trump when the pair meets on Tuesday, arguing for a speedy resolution to the wars in Iran and Ukraine while urging the US to engage in the Indo-Pacific.

The Quad leaders’ summit in the Philippines’ capital of Manila will be Trump’s first, in either of his presidencies. The US president, fresh from a crushing midterms result, will take centre stage in gatherings of Asian leaders and prepare for historic three-way talks with Xi Jinping of China and Russia’s Vladimir Putin this week.

Underlying the diplomatic swing are efforts by the federal government to avoid angering China, as the Quad leaders gather for the first time since 2024 – and after Australia joined countries, including the US and Japan, in an agreement for new protections around key AI technologies.

Designed to firm up supply chains for chips and critical minerals components, the San Francisco Declaration was crafted to promote cooperation in the face of China’s efforts to control areas of AI development.

articles.title: Amazon’s Zoox robotaxis are now available via Uber
articles.summary: Uber may be breaking up with Waymo, but it's also gaining a new robotaxi BFF: Amazon. Starting today, Uber riders in Las Vegas can be matched with Amazon-owned Zoox's purpose-built, bidirectional robotaxis.
body: Riders in Las Vegas can hail Amazon-owned Zoox’s steering-wheel-free robotaxis through the Uber app — with an MGM Resorts partnership and a 2027 Los Angeles expansion on the way.

It’s a first for both companies: the first time Uber is adding a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free autonomous vehicle to its network, and the first time that Zoox is opening up its fleet to a third-party app. Uber says that anyone ordering an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save in Sin City can get matched with a Zoox at no extra charge. Just like with Uber’s other AV partnerships (like Waymo in Phoenix and Austin, for now), riders can toggle a preference in the app’s Ride Preferences settings to boost their chances of getting an autonomous pod.

Unlike Uber’s human drivers, Zoox has some geographic limitations. The company’s robotaxis only cover heavy tourist zones, like the Strip, downtown Las Vegas, and the Arts District. And Zoox isn’t abandoning its standalone app; it will continue to operate independently alongside the Uber integration.

articles.title: Apple MacBook Pro M6 review: probably the last of its generation
articles.summary: Spec bump adds power to exceptionally long battery life in base-model Pro laptop, but is overshadowed by a new design. Apple’s base-model MacBook Pro gets a solid speed bump, offering most of the features from its top-level siblings but in a design that has just been superseded and may soon be…
body: It is the starting model in Apple’s popular MacBook Pro line, but that doesn’t make it cheap. Costing from £1,999 (€2,299/$1,999/A$3,199) it is £300 or equivalent more than its predecessor as RAMageddon continues to jack up prices. It is, at least, £500 cheaper than the other new MacBook Pros.

The laptop’s solid aluminium body, look and feel are identical to its predecessors, using the design first introduced in 2021. With five generations of the machine having been and gone, it is a bit of a known quantity, but the 120Hz miniLED screen is still brilliant, as are the first-class keyboard and trackpad. The port selection is also solid and the MagSafe charging cable remains a delight.

The M6 model only comes with the smaller 14.2in screen, which is still the sweet spot for portability and productivity. It reaches a sustained 1,000nits brightness for standard content and working – double that of the MacBook Air – and hits 1,600nits to make HDR content pop. It is only really beaten by the OLED screen on the new MacBook Pro design, which costs considerably more.

articles.title: UK exposed to polycrisis of threats amid government ‘complacency’
articles.summary: Lords report calls for urgent new approach to resilience planning in face of cyber-attacks, sabotage and climate crisis. Ministers are complacent in the face of fast-changing and increasingly interconnected threats to the UK, and must act quickly to increase national resilience to possibly very…
body: While Labour recently launched a “Be Ready” campaign, advising households to have stocks of food and water, most of the public are unaware of the scale of potential threats from cyber-attacks, proxy acts of violence or strikes on underseas cables, as well as natural disasters such as extreme weather and flooding, it said.

Written by the Lords national resilience committee after months of expert hearings, the report calls for a new and coherent approach to resilience planning, including a dedicated cabinet minister and an annual statement to parliament by the prime minister to set out the extent of preparedness.
It also called for more flexible ways to communicate with the public, including a pause to plans to switch off the Freeview-style digital terrestrial TV signal, in case other systems are disrupted.

Another recommendation is for the government to send every household a booklet setting out how people can prepare for and respond to an emergency, following the model of countries such as Denmark and Sweden.

articles.title: Senator slams Commerce Secretary for flow of Nvidia AI chips to China
articles.summary: Washington Senator Maria Cantwell, one of the top Democrats on the Senate commerce committee, has taken fire at the Department of Commerce (DOC) under Secretary Howard Lutnick for neglecting to enforce protections intended to keep Nvidia's AI chips away from China.
body: Amid the Jensen Huang fallout, Maria Cantwell accuses Howard Lutnick of giving away ‘America’s technology advantage in AI.’

“Despite clear authority from Congress, the Department of Commerce has allowed advanced AI chips to flow through companies with ties to the People’s Republic of China (PRC). The Department of Commerce has resisted efforts to restrict companies flagged as national security threats, weakened safeguards, and left open pathways for the PRC to train advanced AI models using sensitive American technology.”

In her letter, Cantwell specifically calls out instances when the DOC reportedly didn’t heed warnings from White House and intelligence officials to restrict Megaspeed’s access to AI chips, prior to allegations that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a then-Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese spy. Cantwell also criticizes the DOC for allowing Alibaba and ByteDance to access Nvidia chips through overseas data centers, and extending a loophole that let restricted companies obtain American AI technology through subsidiaries.

articles.title: How Sam Bankman-Fried Lost Out on a $35 Billion Jackpot From Anthropic
articles.summary: Sam Bankman-Fried, founder of the crypto firm FTX, leaving federal court in Manhattan in 2022. He was convicted of fraud and is now in federal prison in California.
body: Sam Bankman-Fried, the convicted cryptocurrency fraudster, lives in a 30-person unit at the federal prison in Lompoc, Calif., a barbed-wire compound about a million miles away from his former life as a technology billionaire in the Bahamas.
For the most part, Mr. Bankman-Fried, 34, tries not to think about all the “could-have-beens,” he said on a recent call. But one has become difficult to ignore.

In late 2021, the heyday of his FTX crypto exchange, Mr. Bankman-Fried spent $500 million on a 13.5 percent stake in a little-known artificial intelligence start-up called Anthropic. This week, Anthropic is set for an initial public offering that is expected to value the company at $1.4 trillion, potentially one of the largest Wall Street debuts in history.
At that valuation, Mr. Bankman-Fried’s investment, diluted over several years, would now be worth an eye-watering $35 billion — about the size of FTX’s entire business at its peak.

articles.title: Apple Was Late to Video Podcasts. Now It’s Trying to Catch Up.
articles.summary: They will soon be free to all Apple TV users and will appear on more than 1 billion devices that have the app, including Rokus and smart TVs.
body: Apple helped turbocharge the rise of podcasts two decades ago, but as video podcasts reshape the industry it’s fallen behind competitors like YouTube and Spotify.

Now it’s playing catch up. On Monday, Apple will add a video podcasts section to Apple TV, initially just for testing with developers. They will soon be free to all users even if they don’t pay for Apple’s streaming service and will appear on over 1 billion devices that have the Apple TV app, including Rokus and smart TVs. Apple also plans to increase the number of video podcasts on its regular Podcasts app, where it introduced video nine months ago but has been working to bring some of the biggest shows on board.

“We want podcasts to be available wherever people want to enjoy them — the small screens, big screens,” said Oliver Schusser, a vice president at Apple who oversees services including podcasts, television and music. “It’s really about discovery and helping the creators to reach a new audience. We didn’t approach this in a way that would financially benefit us.”
points: They will soon be free to all Apple TV users and will appear on more than 1 billion devices that have the app, including Rokus and smart TVs.

articles.title: The EPA’s Chemical-Detecting Plane Isn’t Doing Its Job Anymore
articles.summary: The Cessna is flying fewer missions and can no longer provide real-time data to disaster responders as toxic emergencies rise.
body: When an ammonia leak outside a hotel in Weatherford, Oklahoma, injured 74 people last November, the federal government's chemical-detection plane stayed on the ground.
When a fire tore through a Valero refinery in Port Arthur, Texas, in March, the plane sat idle.
And when massive blasts killed two workers at an industrial recycling plant in Toledo, Ohio, in August, it stayed put, despite a fire surrounding tanks of flammable solvents.
“Ten years ago, it would have gone to all of them,” says Mark Thomas, a former EPA official who for years managed the airborne detection effort.

articles.title: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess
articles.summary: AI competitors are catching up to Nvidia—and poised to take advantage of the chaos.
body: Nvidia played a key role enabling the AI gold rush thanks in large part to its recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang. Huang was a master of foreseeing technological changes, investing in chips to train AI earlier than most.

But just as he’s leaving, the company has a growing list of competitors with a range of new, advanced technology breathing down its neck. For Nvidia, where CFO Colette Kress has now taken the reins, the timing isn’t great.

“Everything sold today was designed two-to-three years ago,” says the CEO of a large AI company, who spoke to WIRED on condition of anonymity to avoid hurting business relationships. Kress, or whoever replaces her permanently, will have to chart the course that the chip industry will take two years from now, the CEO says.

Nvidia dominates the market for AI accelerators, capturing 80 percent of sales, according to Silicon Analysis. Longtime nemesis AMD is now making a concerted effort to build competitive AI chips. Its share of the market has crept up from just two percent in 2022 to between 7 and 10 percent in 2026.
points: AI competitors are catching up to Nvidia—and poised to take advantage of the chaos.

articles.title: Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors
articles.summary: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket and 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites fell back to Earth minutes after liftoff Sunday, a crushing setback that will ripple across all sectors of the US space industry.
body: The Vulcan rocket is on contract to launch roughly half of the US military’s national security space missions in the next few years, and Sunday’s mission was the first of 38 Vulcan launches booked by Amazon to build out its network of broadband Internet satellites aimed at competing with SpaceX’s Starlink. Sunday’s failure is expected to ground the rocket for an indefinite period of time.

Vulcan is no stranger to close calls, having overcome failures with its strap-on solid rocket boosters on two of its four previous flights. In each case, the rocket corrected for those problems and continued into orbit to deploy its payloads. The incidents trigged months-long reviews and investigations before ULA could resume Vulcan flights.

Sunday’s launch succumbed to a different kind of failure. The six solid rocket boosters appeared to perform well in the first two minutes after Vulcan’s liftoff from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, at 12:40 pm EDT (17:40 UTC).
